topic: Microsoft AI-103 Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure certification exam preparation - the 2026 successor to AI-102, built around Microsoft Foundry apps and agents
cert_name: Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate
exam_format: Approximately 40-60 questions, 100 minutes, passing score 700/1000, online proctored or test center. Question types include multiple choice, multiple select, drag-and-drop, case studies, and hot area. Associate-level certification renews annually via a free online assessment. AI-103 replaced the retired AI-102 (retired June 30, 2026).
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Azure AI engineers and developers who build, deploy, and manage AI apps and agents with Microsoft Foundry. Candidates should have Python development experience and familiarity with generative AI concepts and Azure services. Ideal next step for students who completed AI-901 or AZ-900.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
domains.notes: Choosing appropriate Foundry services and models (LLMs, small language models, multimodal models, Foundry Tools) for generative tasks, grounding, vector search, agent workflows, and multimodal processing; retrieval and indexing method selection; memory, tool, and knowledge integration services for agents. Setting up AI solutions in Foundry: infrastructure design, deployment options, model and agent deployment configuration, CI/CD integration. Managing, monitoring, and securing AI systems: quotas, scaling, rate limits, cost; model performance, drift, safety events, grounding quality; data ingestion and index health; managed identity, private networking, keyless credentials, role policies. Responsible AI across generative and agentic systems: safety filters, guardrails, risk detection, content moderation, evaluators, trace logging, provenance metadata, approval workflows, agent oversight modes and tool-access controls.

domains.name: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
domains.notes: The heart of the exam. Building generative applications with Foundry: deploying and consuming LLMs, small models, code models, multimodal models; implementing RAG in an application; designing workflows, tool-augmented flows, multistep reasoning pipelines; evaluating models and apps (fabrication detection, relevance, quality, safety); Foundry SDKs and connectors; connecting apps to Foundry projects. Building agents with Foundry: agent roles, goals, conversation tracking, tool schemas; retrieval + function-calling + conversation memory; agent tools (APIs, knowledge stores, search, Content Understanding, custom functions); orchestrated multi-agent solutions; autonomous and semiautonomous workflows with safeguards and approval flows; agent monitoring, evaluation, and error analysis. Optimizing and operationalizing: prompt engineering, model parameters, model reflection, chain-of-thought evaluations, self-critique loops, tracing, token analytics, latency breakdowns, orchestrating multiple models and hybrid LLM plus rules-engine designs.

domains.name: Implement computer vision solutions
domains.notes: Image and video GENERATION (new emphasis vs AI-102): generating images and videos from text prompts and reference media, image-editing workflows (inpainting, mask-based edits, prompt-driven modifications), video editing workflows, generation and editing controls. Multimodal understanding: analyzing visual context with multimodal models, captioning, visual question answering grounded in visual evidence, alt-text generation for accessibility, Azure Content Understanding for visual characteristics, video analysis workflows, single-task and pro-mode Content Understanding pipelines, object/component/region identification. Responsible AI for multimodal content: unsafe visual content filters, indirect prompt injection via embedded text in images, watermarks, prohibited-symbol flagging, brand usage rules.

domains.name: Implement text analysis solutions
domains.notes: Language model text analysis: extracting entities, topics, summaries, and structured JSON outputs with generative prompting and Foundry Tools; sentiment, tone, safety, and sensitive-content detection; translation with Azure Translator in Foundry Tools or LLM-powered flows; customizing outputs for domain tasks like compliance summarization. Speech solutions: speech-to-text and text-to-speech for agentic interactions, speech as an agent modality including custom speech models, multimodal reasoning from audio inputs, speech translation with language models and Foundry Tools.

domains.name: Implement information extraction solutions
domains.notes: Retrieval and grounding pipelines: ingesting and indexing documents, images, audio, and video; semantic, hybrid, and vector search for grounding; enrichment with custom or built-in skills; RAG ingestion flow including OCR; connecting retrieval pipelines to workflows and agent tools. Document extraction: multimodal pipelines combining OCR, layout analysis, and field extraction; producing clean grounded representations for agents and RAG with Content Understanding; analyzers generating structured or markdown outputs for downstream reasoning.

extra_guidance: AI-103 is the successor to the retired AI-102 and is considered the flagship exam of Microsoft's 2026 AI certification wave - marketing angle: 'built for the NEW AI-103, not a recycled AI-102 course'. The five domain names and weights above are Microsoft's official skills-measured outline (as of April 16, 2026) - use them verbatim. Key shifts from AI-102 that the course must reflect: (1) agents are now first-class and woven through every domain, not a 5-10% afterthought - Microsoft Foundry Agent Service and Microsoft Agent Framework get deep coverage; (2) computer vision now emphasizes image/video GENERATION and multimodal understanding rather than classic custom vision training; (3) knowledge mining is reframed as retrieval/grounding for RAG and agents; (4) everything is Microsoft Foundry-branded (formerly Azure AI Foundry) - use current naming with a one-line note about the rename. Audience is developers: code samples in Python with the Foundry SDK at read-and-understand level, focusing on which API/service/pattern to choose rather than syntax memorization. Natural upsell funnel from the AI-901 course - reference that fundamentals are assumed, not retaught. Labs: Foundry portal walkthroughs (deploy model, create agent, wire up a tool, run an evaluation), RAG pipeline sketch with Azure AI Search vector/hybrid modes, Content Understanding analyzer setup. Practice tests must include scenario/case-study style questions: choosing between deployment options, picking retrieval strategies, diagnosing grounding failures, selecting responsible AI controls (prompt shields vs content filters vs blocklists), and agent orchestration trade-offs. Cover classic traps: managed identity vs keys, provisioned vs serverless deployment, semantic vs vector vs hybrid search, Content Understanding vs Document Intelligence, when to use Agent Service vs plain chat completion. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation walkthrough with 100-minute time-management strategy including case-study pacing.
